slots.practicalActivity: In your Trailhead Playground, open the App Launcher and tour at least 3 existing apps, then open Setup's App Manager and identify, for one app, its tabs, branding, navigation order, and which profiles can see it.
slots.deliverable: A written breakdown of one existing app's 4 bundled pieces (tabs, branding, navigation order, visibility) as found in App Manager.

slots.practicalActivity: In App Manager, click New Lightning App and build a custom app named Warranty Service Console: set its name/icon/color in Details, move at least 4 items into Navigation Items in a deliberate order, and assign it to a profile in User Profiles.
slots.deliverable: One new custom Lightning app (Warranty Service Console) with 4+ ordered navigation items, visible in the App Launcher.

slots.practicalActivity: Before building anything else, answer the Who/What/Why/Scale questions in writing for a warranty-claims tracking requirement, then walk the declarative-first design order (reuse object, reuse field, configure, customize, ask 'does this exist already') to reach your first design decision.
slots.deliverable: A written Who/What/Why/Scale analysis plus a documented first design decision for a warranty-claims requirement, following the declarative-first order.

slots.practicalActivity: On paper, list the nouns in the warranty-claims requirement (Claim, Asset, Product, Customer), mark each parent/child relationship, identify which one is many-to-many, and sketch the resulting entity-relationship diagram including any junction object it needs.
slots.deliverable: A written entity-relationship sketch for the warranty-claims model, naming each object, each relationship's shape (one-to-many or many-to-many), and any junction object required.

slots.practicalActivity: In Object Manager, create Warranty_Claim__c with a Label, Plural Label, and API Name, add a Master-Detail Relationship field related to the standard Asset object, save it, and confirm a Warranty Claims related list now appears automatically on an Asset record.
slots.deliverable: One new custom object (Warranty_Claim__c) with a master-detail relationship to Asset, confirmed by its related list appearing on an Asset record.

slots.practicalActivity: Add Warranty_Claim__c's 5 deliberate fields from the lesson (Claim_Number__c Auto Number, Claim_Date__c Date required, Status__c Picklist New/Review/Approved/Denied, Resolution_Notes__c Long Text Area, and a placeholder for Total_Claimed__c), running the 4-question pass (type, constraint, who edits, who sees) for each.
slots.deliverable: Warranty_Claim__c with 5 fields added, each documented against the 4-question field-design pass (type, constraint, edit access, visibility).

slots.practicalActivity: Independently design and build a second custom object and relationship for a different requirement you invent (not warranty claims), running the same Who/What/Why/Scale questions, entity-relationship sketch, and field-design pass before touching Object Manager.
slots.deliverable: A second, independently designed custom object with at least one relationship and 3+ deliberately-typed fields, plus the written requirements and ER-sketch work that preceded building it.

slots.practicalActivity: Review your Warranty_Claim__c object end to end against the chapter's design order: confirm you reused standard objects and fields wherever possible, state in writing why master-detail (not lookup) was the correct relationship choice, and identify one thing you'd change if claim volume scaled to 50,000 records a year.
slots.deliverable: A written design-review document justifying your relationship choice and identifying one scale-driven change to the warranty-claims data model.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a second Page Layout for Warranty_Claim__c with a different field arrangement, assign it to a specific profile via Page Layout Assignment, then separately build a Compact Layout with up to 10 priority-ordered fields, set it primary, and confirm it powers the highlights panel.
slots.deliverable: 2 Page Layouts on Warranty_Claim__c (one profile-assigned) plus one primary Compact Layout confirmed in the record's highlights panel.

slots.practicalActivity: In Lightning App Builder, create a new App Page for the Warranty Service Console app, drag in a list view component and a report chart component, configure each in the right-hand panel, and activate the page as the app's home page.
slots.deliverable: One activated Lightning App Builder App Page, serving as the Warranty Service Console's home page, with 2 configured components.

slots.practicalActivity: Migrate Warranty_Claim__c's record page to Dynamic Forms using the migration wizard, then add a component visibility rule so the Resolution_Notes__c field only renders when Status__c is Approved or Denied.
slots.deliverable: A Dynamic Forms-migrated Warranty_Claim__c record page with one field-level visibility rule, tested by changing Status__c.

slots.practicalActivity: Create one Global Action (for example New Warranty Claim, reachable from the header plus icon with no record context) and one object-specific Quick Action scoped to Warranty_Claim__c (for example Escalate Claim), then confirm where each one actually appears in the UI.
slots.deliverable: One Global Action and one object-specific Quick Action, each confirmed working from its correct location (header plus icon vs. record action menu).

slots.practicalActivity: Drag a standard component (such as a Related List or Report Chart) onto the Warranty Service Console's App Page alongside any custom Lightning web component available in your org, and document which exposed properties you were able to configure without writing code.
slots.deliverable: The Warranty Service Console App Page updated with one additional component, plus a written list of its configurable exposed properties.

lessons.title: Mobile and the Salesforce Mobile App

slots.practicalActivity: Open the Warranty Service Console in the Salesforce mobile app (or the mobile preview in Lightning App Builder), review the Menu screen's item order, then use the app's Activation dialog's Mobile Navigation tab to set a mobile-specific order different from the desktop nav bar, putting Warranty Claims first.
slots.deliverable: A Warranty Service Console app with a Mobile Navigation order set independently of its desktop nav bar, confirmed in the mobile preview.

slots.practicalActivity: Independently build a complete interface pass for the second custom object created in Chapter 1's practice slot: 2 page layouts, a compact layout, a Dynamic Forms migration with one visibility rule, and one quick action, without reusing Warranty_Claim__c's configuration as a template.
slots.deliverable: A second object with a full, independently built interface stack (2 page layouts, compact layout, Dynamic Forms visibility rule, quick action).

slots.practicalActivity: Write a one-page UI walkthrough of the finished Warranty Service Console app as if onboarding a new dispatcher: what they see first, which fields are hidden until which status, and how the experience differs on mobile.
slots.deliverable: A written onboarding walkthrough document describing the Warranty Service Console's interface, field visibility behavior, and mobile differences.

slots.practicalActivity: Before building any logic, write out Salesforce's save order from memory (system validations, validation rules, before-save Apex, save, after-save automation, Flow), then map which of the 5 business-logic tools you'll use for Warranty_Claim__c and why, before opening any tool.
slots.deliverable: A written save-order diagram plus a documented plan mapping validation rules, formula fields, roll-up summaries, and approval processes/Flow to specific Warranty_Claim__c requirements.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a validation rule on Warranty_Claim__c blocking a save when Status__c is Approved and Resolution_Notes__c is blank, using ISPICKVAL and ISBLANK, write a clear error message with Error Location on Resolution_Notes__c, and test it against a record that should fail and one that should pass.
slots.deliverable: One active validation rule on Warranty_Claim__c, confirmed to block an invalid save and allow a valid one.

slots.practicalActivity: Add a Formula field on Warranty_Claim__c (for example Days_Since_Claim__c, Number, using TODAY() and Claim_Date__c) and a second cross-object formula pulling a field from the related Asset through dot notation, confirming both calculate correctly and are read-only.
slots.deliverable: 2 formula fields on Warranty_Claim__c: one calculated from its own fields, and one cross-object formula reaching the related Asset.

lessons.title: Roll-Up Summary Fields and Junction Objects

slots.practicalActivity: Build Total_Claimed__c as a Roll-Up Summary field (SUM) on the parent object, aggregating a numeric field from Warranty_Claim__c's detail records with a filter excluding Cancelled line items, then confirm it recalculates when a detail record is added, edited, or deleted.
slots.deliverable: One working Roll-Up Summary field with a filter condition, confirmed to recalculate correctly on detail-record changes.

lessons.title: Approval Processes and Flow for Apps

slots.practicalActivity: Build an Approval Process on Warranty_Claim__c with entry criteria Total_Claimed__c greater than a chosen threshold, one approval step routing to a specific approver, and a final-approval field update, then build a simple screen Flow capable of triggering Submit for Approval based on logic the entry criteria alone couldn't express.
slots.deliverable: One working Approval Process with entry criteria and an approval step, plus one screen Flow capable of submitting a record for approval.

slots.practicalActivity: Take 4 of your own Warranty_Claim__c requirements (one that should block, one that should calculate, one that should aggregate, one that should route for approval) and run each through the lesson's decision path, confirming your Chapter 3 build already matches the resulting tool choice.
slots.deliverable: A written decision-path walkthrough for 4 requirements, confirming each maps to the validation rule, formula field, roll-up summary, or approval process already built.

slots.practicalActivity: Independently add one new business-logic requirement to Warranty_Claim__c that composes at least 2 tools together (for example a roll-up summary feeding a validation rule's threshold, or a Flow evaluating conditions before calling Submit for Approval), designing it yourself with no lesson-by-lesson steps.
slots.deliverable: One new, independently designed requirement on Warranty_Claim__c implemented with 2+ composed business-logic tools, documented with the reasoning behind the composition.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a Summary report on Warranty_Claim__c grouped by Status__c with Sum of Total_Claimed__c, then a Matrix report crossing Status__c by a second field, and embed one as a Report Chart component directly on the Warranty Service Console's app page from Lesson 10.
slots.deliverable: A Summary report and a Matrix report on Warranty_Claim__c, with one embedded directly as a live component on the Warranty Service Console app page.

slots.practicalActivity: Set Warranty_Claim__c's Organization-Wide Default to Private, build a dedicated Warranty Claims Access permission set granting object and field access, add one sharing rule for a predictable exception (for example a support queue), and confirm a test user without the permission set cannot see the object tab at all.
slots.deliverable: Warranty_Claim__c secured with Private OWD, a dedicated permission set, one sharing rule, and a confirmed test showing a user without the permission set has no object access.

slots.practicalActivity: If a sandbox is available in your Trailhead or Developer setup, create an Outbound Change Set containing Warranty_Claim__c, its fields, the validation rule, and the roll-up summary, add any dependencies the validation step flags, and walk through Validate before Deploy; otherwise document the full outbound/inbound steps and dependency list in writing instead.
slots.deliverable: One Outbound Change Set populated with Warranty_Claim__c's components and dependencies, either actually validated/deployed or fully documented step by step.

slots.practicalActivity: Add field-level help text to at least 3 Warranty_Claim__c fields, create an In-App Guidance Prompt introducing the Escalate quick action on the Warranty Service Console's page, and draft a phased rollout plan (pilot permission set group first) for a fictional dispatch team.
slots.deliverable: 3 fields with added help text, one configured In-App Guidance Prompt, and a written phased-rollout plan for a pilot user group.

slots.practicalActivity: Re-read the Harborline Logistics case study and, against your own Warranty Service Console build, write a matching decision table: your Chapter 1 data-model decisions, Chapter 2 UI decisions, Chapter 3 logic decisions, and Chapter 4 delivery decisions, each traced to the specific lesson that justified it.
slots.deliverable: A written decision table tracing your own app's Chapter 1-4 decisions to specific lessons, structured like the Harborline Logistics case study.

slots.practicalActivity: Treat Warranty_Claim__c as finished and confirm, end to end, that every piece from this course is actually in place: object/fields, page layout plus compact layout plus Dynamic Forms, validation rule plus formula plus roll-up plus approval process, and OWD/permission set/report/change-set/adoption plan, filling any gap you find.
slots.deliverable: A completed Warranty Service Console app with every Chapter 1-4 piece confirmed present, and a written gap-closure note for anything added at this final check.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a second complete small application from scratch end to end - data model, interface, business logic, and delivery - on a new requirement you invent (not warranty claims), completing all 4 steps with no lesson-by-lesson guidance, the same way the Help Desk Ticket example did in Lesson 24.
slots.deliverable: A second, fully built complete application (new object model, interface, business logic, and delivery/security setup) built independently end to end.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a final course retrospective comparing your 2 complete app builds (Warranty Service Console and your Lesson 30 app): which design decisions you made faster the second time, and a checklist you'd hand a new Platform App Builder for their first build.
slots.deliverable: A final written retrospective comparing both app builds, plus an original first-build checklist for a new Platform App Builder.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student can design and build a complete custom Salesforce application from scratch: a reuse-first data model with the right relationship types, a Lightning app with Dynamic Forms and quick actions, validation rules, formulas, roll-ups, and approval processes composed into working business logic, and a secured, reported-on, deployed, and adopted application ready for real users.
